current.text: Miami acquired Giannis Antetokounmpo. Miami lacks other point guards and ball handlers, so Giannis is expected to handle the ball a lot and may run point.
He is Miami's current starting point guard. He is in the projected starting five, which one expert gives about a 75% chance.
With Giannis handling the ball, his assists and his already low usage should drop. He may not start, may not close games, and could be a 27-minute player even as a starter.
Experts fade him at his market price. Do not take him around 110 to 118. He is a last-round pick at most, around round 15.
Miami has a weak 4-3-3 schedule in our fantasy playoff weeks, which is 10 games.
Miami has 13 back-to-backs, the fewest in the league.

durable.text: He is a very low-usage player and not a scorer. His value in categories comes almost only from assists.
He is weak in free throws, rebounds and blocks, and he makes few threes.
Experts disagree on his steals. Some call them good, others say he does not get enough or gets none.
He has shot about 40% from three in each of the last two seasons, but on very low volume.
His efficiency has improved, but one expert does not trust his shooting at higher volume.

note: He is a fringe player for us. Yahoo values him at 3 USD (rank 112) and ESPN at 0 USD (rank 176), and the experts say to fade him at that price because Giannis should cut into his assists, his only strong category (6.6 projected per game). He is at best a 1 USD last-round pick for an assist-hungry build, and he hurts FT%, rebounds and points. In the first weeks, check whether he starts and closes games next to Giannis and whether his assists hold near 6 per game.
